factions.name: The Crown
themes: Lineage, bloodlines, ancestry and the shadow of the past.
Quests, chivalry, burdensome duties and dire obligations.
Tarnished grandeur, relics and the remnants of empire.
Gold, stone, dust and crimson cloth.
factions.description:
An ancient tradition forcing the Isles back into a mythical golden era.
A legendary past enshrouds the Isles. Before smokestacks and presses, before looms and workhouses, before cutting-edge science and an empire that spanned the globe, the Isles were a place of quiet majesty. Of noble knights, gleaming armour, slain dragons and momentous destinies. The Crown clings to this ingrained mythology tighter each decade, and as the country falls into disrepair and chaos, it redoubles its efforts to be perceived as an ancient and worthy tradition worth keeping.
As the empire collapses in upon itself and old enemies rise to attack its borders, the Crown has all but abandoned the technological advances that saw the Isles conquer the world first with war and then with trade. The Crown and its subsidiaries still run the military, and are keen to turn back the clock to a time when might was the only power that mattered.
Campaigns are steered at the whims of backstabbing nobles, the politics of the court, and the whispered words of a hundred viziers, schemers, occultists and sages. Knight-Sergeants lead units into battle wearing outdated hereditary platemail and carrying heavy swords. Soldiers claim to trace their lineage or tradition to some great battle or another, etch their ancestry into their weapons, and swap tales of inherited glory around dying campfires.
Even this imitation of power can't last. The Crown knows that the next war they fight will be a civil one, and they hope there will be a country left to rule over when the dust settles.
factions.hollows:
The Crown believes it is their sworn duty to defend the Isles from attack, and if they get to do that by slaying some sort of great beast, so much the better. Unfortunately, their normal method of getting a large number of poor people to do the work for them has failed, as few can successfully enter a Hollow and hope to emerge again.
On occasion a noble of noteworthy standing will be cursed with a Seed and take up the mantle of Hunter themselves, but a life of being waited on hand and foot does little to prepare them for the harsh unrealities of a Hollow.
factions.weapons:
The Sword a symbol of wealth, power and self-determination is chief amongst the tools of the Crown, although recently they have taken up the Pistol as a more modern equivalent. The Armour is also a fond favourite, thanks to its mythic connections. Of course that's for the nobles, and if they're lucky the Knights-Sergeant. Soldiers carry Rifles and Bludgeons and die in the mud, and they should be bloody grateful for the opportunity.
Crown Weapons often bear inscriptions, filigree and grips made of unusual materials hinting at the influence that the empire once held: obsidian hauled from sweltering jungles, ivory torn from the beasts of the savanna, gold from a hundred tithing nations. Knightly relics such as fingerbones, shards of armour, or pennants are worked into or bound around Weapons to invoke the martial prowess of fallen warriors.

origins.name: Blueblood
origins.text:
Petty nobles under pressure from their family.
As the Isles crumble and the nation tilts towards chaos, the ruling
classes have retreated to lives of mouldering luxury and with
fewer and fewer friends each year, only the most powerful and
firmly entrenched nobles stand a chance of survival. You were the
scion of one of these families, and they placed all their hopes upon
your back. It didn't work out as well as they'd wanted. Maybe your
family is clinging to power by a thread, and are one bad harvest
away from losing their lands; maybe they're deep in debt and frantic
to find any way out of it. Or maybe your failings were what doomed
them, and you are the final rank of a once-fruitful family tree.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: stand on
ceremony, refer to the glorious if chequered history of the Isles, dress
up, impress the middle-classes, and so on.

origins.name: Chamberlain
origins.text:
Household staff sworn to serve their betters.
Your parents served the Crown. Their parents served the Crown,
and their parents before them, and if you were the sort of family
that could afford to document their ancestry, you would witness a
lineage stretching back into antiquity parallel to the royal line. But
you're not. You're dirt poor, and now the Crown is tarnished and
worn, you no longer command what little respect you once held.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: tidy up, blend in,
do as you're told, exact quiet revenge, and so on.

origins.name: Knight-Sergeant
origins.text:
Squad leaders who work hard to be respected.
Becoming a Knight is one of the few ways that a commoner can
stand adjacent to, if not strictly amongst, the echelons of the royal
family. By proving one's worth in battle for the Isles and leading the
legions of its conquering troops, even someone of ignoble birth is
granted authority and standing. That's what you were told, anyway.
In reality, you're thrust into a world of politics you couldn't give a
damn about, none of the soldiers will go for a drink with you any
more, and you're held responsible for every error your troops make.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: give orders,
inspire bravery, look out for danger, and so on.

origins.name: Regimental Peon
origins.text:
Cannon-fodder in the Crown infantry.
Boundaries, borders and kings be damned; you are the Isles. You
and yours have fought and died for generations to keep this place
safe. (Not that it's safe any more.) Your ancestors knew what it
meant to be part of something great, and they bound their blood to
the Crown. That blood runs in you still whether you like it or not,
and everyone expects you to do your duty. Maybe you were honour-
branded when you came of age to remind you, and everyone else, of
the promises sworn on your behalf: promises that you felt powerless
either to escape or to uphold.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: withstand
horrible conditions, march for hours, stand in the rain, and so on.

seeds.name: Abolitionist
seeds.text:
Something made you want to tear it all down.
You felt resentment growing on the streets each day. You found
others who thought like you and dreamed of a better world, and
you did what you could to make that world a reality. Then:
l Your royalist family discovered your intentions and tried to hand you over to the Crown.
l You incited a riot which burned a tenement to the ground, killing dozens.
l You took the life of a royal, and had to disappear. l Agents of the Crown rooted out your revolutionary cell and made
an example of your comrades.

seeds.name: Deserter
seeds.text:
You ran from your duty, and people got hurt.
Whether a soldier, a noble, a servant or a peon, every member of
society has a place within the Crown's domain if they uphold their
duty. You did not uphold your duty; you betrayed the trust of people
who were relying on you. Nothing has been the same ever since you:
l Got drunk on watch, passed out, and let enemy skirmishers ambush your squadmates.
l Married for love, not for standing, and watched your family name crumble to dust.
l Were caught smuggling your child out of the regimental grounds so they wouldn't be drafted for life.
l Sent your squad forward into a trap and hid from danger instead of warning them.

seeds.name: Murderer
seeds.text:
You killed someone you shouldn't have.
People kill each other all the time. Disputes over control of territory,
frustration at infidelity or insubordination, and Friday night gin-
brawls are all staples of life in the Isles. For young people looking
for work in the industrial shanties, getting your head kicked in is
just an occupational hazard (and one that some people relish using
as leverage). But things were different when you killed:
l A noble, with powerful and vengeful connections. l Your sibling, in a fit of rage that passed and left you filled with regret. l Your officer, after she issued an order that got your squad killed. l Your son, after you discovered what he did at night.

seeds.name: Sole Survivor
seeds.text:
Everyone died, except you.
The new power blocs of the Isles scramble
to strip influence from the dying Crown.
Noble houses are wiped off the map with
the stroke of a pen, or in secret with fire
and shot; desperate troops are denied
reinforcements as commanders shelter in
bunkers; household staff are driven from
their homes and starve in the streets when
their masters are deposed. You were the
only survivor after:
l Your regiment was drawn into a Hollow and unable to escape.
l Infidelity, and a dinner party massacre, left you the last member of your family alive.
l The staff of a cruel household were all but wiped out in a month from a coughing sickness.
l Your second squad was massacred, and you were discharged after being deemed bad luck.

factions.name: The House
themes: Cities, ports, ruins and abandoned places.
factions.description:
A people's government bound by bureaucracy and tilting toward civil war.
About a century ago, following pressure from industrialists and exporters, the Crown graciously granted the common folk the right to rule themselves under democratic process and (with great reluctance) nationalised vast swathes of the manufacturing sector. For the first time in written history, over half the Isles were collectively owned by the people who lived and worked there, and no longer under the draconian thrall of a distant monarch. Elected officials worked to better the lives of their constituents, profits were reinvested in the community, and far fewer labourers died due to unsafe machinery or starved to death in the gutter.
Then: the empire collapsed, the work dried up, exports were sunk or blockaded, armies lost war after war on foreign soil, and the House began to cannibalise itself to stay functional. Frantic contracts, desperate promises and vicious threats carved the corpse of the Isles into bloody fragments that changed hands on a monthly basis. A new echelon of Islander arose in the professional politician, proudly severed from the Crown and fiercely working-class, but just as concerned with clinging desperately to power and internecine conflict as the nobles whose rule they refused.
Now, the House is divided into a dozen seats of influence centred around the little industrial infrastructure that remains in the Isles. Responsible for the lives of several million citizens, they function no differently to any other protection racket, although they take pride in citing laws and edicts to back up their violence. In the halls of power, Ministers whisper: the Crown is weak, and their weakness lost them the empire. They damned this country to rust and ruin and they ought to pay. In the streets, tensions rise as gangs of House militia clash with those loyal to the Crown.
The Isles are on the brink of civil war, and the House is hungry for blood.
factions.hollows: There are no end of explanations for the rapid decline of the Isles into fractious chaos, and many of them place the blame squarely at the feet of the House's rivals: the insular Viridians, the money-sink that is the Crown, or the meddling weirdos in the Conclave all form convenient scapegoats. The majority of the House have bought into their own propaganda or can't afford to question it too deeply but a devoted core of like-minded obsessives have uncovered the truth behind the infectious corruption, and fight a quiet war to burn it out of the country. Teams of House-sponsored Hunters infiltrate communities on the brink of collapse, with instructions to locate and seal any Hollows they find. These violent and unregulated bands of mercenaries often do more harm than good.
factions.weapons: After centuries of the Crown controlling the spread of weapons through the Isles for fear of revolution, the House leapt at the chance to arm every citizen in the nation as an expression of their personal freedom. While the new, mass-produced models of gun, blade and club were less elegant and refined than their handmade ancestors, they were a lot cheaper, and they were perfectly capable of killing any royalist who poked their nose in where it didn't belong. Hunters hailing from the House often use these same bargain-basement Weapons, each well-loved and modified by the bearer the Shotgun, the Pistol, the Knife and the Bludgeon all play a part.

origins.name: Agent
origins.text:
Armed enforcers, guards and petty tyrants.
Each member of Parliament is permitted by law to maintain a small
militia company who protect their interests and enforce House
regulations. As tensions in the Isles have mounted, the exact legal
definition of a "small company" has been stretched to breaking
point; while most bureaucrats might have an agent or two, senior
ministers have been known to employ hundreds of guards to ensure
their will is carried out. You were in the employ of the House and
you enforced its edicts with blood.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: intimidate the little
people, stand watch for hours on end, escalate a situation, and so on.

origins.name: Labourer
origins.text:
Multitudes sweating and dying in state-owned factories.
The industrialisation of the Isles was not kind to labourers, but the
life of the average factory worker was better during the heyday of the
empire than it is now. Bereft of capital and beset by Hollows, industrial
regions all over the country fall into dangerous states of disrepair.
Opportunistic bureaucrats hungry for overseas contracts sell cheap
labour in scrapped-together firetraps and condemn hundreds to
early deaths with the stroke of a pen. You worked in such a place
probably dozens of them and you have the scars to prove it.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: bodge together a
just-workable solution, keep your head down, grit your teeth through
the pain, and so on.

origins.name: Minister
origins.text:
Grasping at the bottom rung of the political ladder.
The House is an interwoven network of hierarchies, obligations and
debts that is inscrutable to most; you were sharp enough to get your
foot in the door. Maybe you were born into money and greased the
right palms, or maybe you pulled yourself up by your bootstraps, but
once you secured your office one thing became clear: no-one was going
to give you a fucking inch. Years of sleepless nights and dubious moral
choices earned you nothing more than a better class of enemy.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: find the loophole,
bring someone round to your point of view, conceal the truth, and so on.

origins.name: Professional
origins.text:
Change the world at the stroke of a pen.
Close in the wake of the rise of the machines came the rise of the
managers. As capitalists and warriors marshalled men to achieve great
ends, administrators and bureaucrats helped turn their commands
into plans. Step by incremental step, rules and regulations emerged
from the chaos along with their creator-followers: lawyers, accountants,
teachers, tax collectors, civil servants and the countless other fussy,
meticulous beancounters that meet in convivial associations to hear
speeches, commiserate over their bosses, and make the world tick
over. You were one of them: your hands are soft, your heart is hard,
and you know what it's like to swallow pride, rage and desire down,
day after day, to make someone else's dreams come true.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: use the rules to
get what you want, offer self-serving counsel, subsume fury into precise
action, and so on.

seeds.name: Betrayer
seeds.text:
You turned against those who relied on you.
The House holds loyalty in low regard; trust is something to be
extracted from a patsy rather than placed in a dear friend. You
usually had no compunction against turning on those closest to you,
but you never recovered after you:
l Planted evidence so one of your underlings was hanged for crimes that you committed.
l Drunkenly confessed your infidelities to your husband, who used them to blackmail you.
l Embezzled thousands of pounds from your employer, doomed your factory, and left hundreds hungry.
l Slipped up, and when your wife found out that you were drinking again after all your promises to stop, she left you.

seeds.name: Class Traitor
seeds.text:
You stepped outside of your station.
Any good Islander knows that their country is a great and impossibly
complex machine, and what keeps it in functional order is the rigid
adherence to class. The circumstances of a citizen's birth, sex, upbringing,
profession and marriage all combine to create a place for them
within the class system, and venturing outside of your pre-ordained
constraints is a recipe for disaster. Things were never the same after:
l You debased yourself before a noble court for the chance to join, and they laughed you out of town.
l Your workmates found your poetry, read it aloud before the first shift, and beat the tar out of you for writing it.
l You married for love, they died penniless, and your social-climber family turned their backs on you.
l They uncovered your records, and found out that you had funded the royalists that stormed the barracks.

seeds.name: Criminal
seeds.text:
You broke the law and got caught.
When the Crown was the sole administrator of justice
in the Isles, any nearby noble could pass sentence on
an offender as they saw fit, and most of them favoured
exile or death. The House generally prefers to keep
criminals alive outside of grievous offences such
as murder, for which they are often executed and
puts them to work in terrible conditions in exchange
for their room and board. You were caught,
convicted and press-ganged into labour after:
l You (unintentionally, your lawyer proved) killed your best friend when you shoved them during an argument and they cracked their head open on the fireplace.
l Protesting against your working conditions, you sabotaged machinery in your workplace and people got seriously hurt.
l They took your child away, and her foster parents reported you for breaking into their house.
l You put three men in the hospital after they hassled you in the street, but one of them was the County Minister's son.

seeds.name: Scapegoat
seeds.text:
Someone had to take the fall.
Everyone has something to hide. You made the
mistake of upsetting someone in charge or
simply being too exploitable to ignore. In an effort
to divert attention away from their own mistakes or
to exact revenge, your superiors made something
public you'd desperately hoped you could keep
secret. Your life was ruined after:
l Your boss pinned the blame for a gruesome industrial accident solely on your head.
l Your County Minister revealed your opium addiction to the gutter press after you tried to oust her from power.
l You were thrown in prison for your part in a murder, whilst everyone else walked free.
l The women in town revealed your love affair (and child) with someone outside of your class.

factions.name: The Temple
themes: Gardening, farming, care and attention given over a long time.
factions.description:
A flourishing religious movement that preaches endless bounty.
The Isles have a long and uneasy relationship with the supernatural. Before the rise of the empire, the average Islander believed that a pantheon of malevolent gods and spirits were ever-ready to punish them for obscure transgressions against inscrutable laws. Ramshackle amalgamations of folk beliefs coalesced into a broad tradition of fear, obfuscation and appeasement; churches were not places to honour the gods, but carefully-maintained divine blind spots where important events (births, marriages, festivals, funerals) could be safely conducted out of their sight.
The empire smashed it all asunder. The relentless march of industrialisation upturned the fragmentary faith. War, hungry for sacrifice, sent whole villages to the front and unattended churches fell to ruin.
The upstart gardeners of the Viridian Temple seized the moment: they preached that the gods were not vicious creatures, but instead dead and rotting beneath the ground, providing sustenance for the world to come. Heaven was no distant realm of light or chthonic purgatory but could rise from the earth itself with careful guidance.
An uprooted populace, battered and bruised from millennia of terror, were ready for a new message. Viridian Temple Gardens sprang up all across the Isles in the lost farms and villages, amidst the smoke and fire of cities, on rooftop and ship deck, in the ruins of fallen churches and behind each fresh military expansion overseas. Viridian morality plays and holy texts flooded the market with the good word. Temple schools taught children to read and write and fed them, and clothed them, and burned the prophecies of plenty into their malleable minds.
Now, the majority of the food supply for the Isles is controlled by the Viridians. The other factions in power don't always see eye to eye with the gardeners, but they toe the line. More than one political enemy has been buried under an orchard, chopped up and fed to sacred pigs, or bonfire-burnt like a parasite weed.
factions.hollows: As the gods rot beneath the soil, their metaphysical putrefaction escapes and catches in this earthly kingdom to form Hollows tenacious and invasive weeds that must be plucked before they take root and spread in the minds and bodies of the congregation. While the majority of the faithful don't give much credence to the existence of parasite dimensions, someone in the upper ranks certainly does, as the church has instituted an aggressive outreach program with an eye to monitoring those at risk of blossoming into something terrible. Whether the sufferer is brought back into the fold or quietly removed, prevention is seen to be better than cure and employing teams of Hunters to demolish Hollows is the sign of a church that failed to do its duty.
factions.weapons:
Traditional tools of farming and animal husbandry turned to violent ends, or modified to be more dangerous, are popular amongst adherents to the Viridian faith. The Knife, the Staff, the Bludgeon and the Spear are all common Weapons amongst their number, and when it comes to ending the life of an injured or belligerent beast, the Shotgun is often the kindest method. Bearers will often augment or modify their Weapons with materials taken from the natural world skulls, thorns, leathers, wool and flowers are common decorations.
The Book is also present in the form of sacred texts that speak of dominion over the natural world and contain useful guidance on crop rotation, care of livestock, treating most common diseases and, of course, performing actual magic spells.

origins.name: Faithful
origins.text:
Devoted members of the congregation.
Worship of the land is the most prevalent faith in the Isles, and most
folks will be involved somehow: paying tithes, volunteering labour or
expertise, or attending garden temple ceremonies a few times a month.
But you devoted your life wholesale to the church, and worked full-
time in one or more farms maybe you never left your town of birth
and tended the soil of the associated land, or maybe you took up the
mantle of pilgrim and followed seasonal work across the country.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: perform back-
breaking labour, stay on your feet for hours on end, work with plants
and livestock, and so on.

origins.name: Revivalist
origins.text:
Garden vanguards seeking wellsprings of potential.
The seeds of Viridianism don't spread themselves. Revivalists like you
were tasked with establishing new garden temples amidst the ruins of
the Isles clutching a green-budded cutting from the great tree that
grows in the high church at Farrow, you cut your previous bonds and
stepped out into the wilderness in search of fertile land. You might
have established a dozen new gardens in the blasted wastes, bringing
prosperity to the malnourished and desperate or you might
have focused instead on destabilising weak communities, driving
recalcitrants out of their homes, and setting down roots by force.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: break and enter,
nourish and nurture, forge ahead on your own, and so on.

origins.name: Swineherd
origins.text:
Itinerant holy folk in charge of sacred beasts.
The domesticated pig is held in the highest regard by the Viridians a
perfect omnivorous beast, fat from the bounty of the land, ripe and
ready for the slaughter. Orthodox adherents proclaim that pigs should
not be kept behind fences or cages but instead allowed to roam the
country as they please, eating unobstructed, and permitted access
to whatever field, storehouse or pantry they barge their way into.
You were a Swineherd, a well-respected and enviable position within
the church, and you spent years wandering the land and contemplating
the divine corpulence and ineffable wisdom of your charges.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: interact with
animals, get up to your elbows in mud and shit, persuade someone to
let you into their private land, etc.

origins.name: Vindicator
origins.text:
Returning the wicked and their gardens of sin to the soil.
Farming is made as much of death as it is growth. Weeds should
be scoured out lest they overgrow crops and sap the life from the
soil; weak plants must be pulled and composted to let their stronger
brothers flourish, and unwanted flowers pruned away; disease and
blight can send whole fields to the bonfire so as not to infect others.
You were a Vindicator for the Temple, and you performed these
same doleful duties upon the people and places of the Isles deemed
unsuitable execution, destruction, absolution and rebirth.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: interrogate and
pry, quietly murder people, dig six-foot holes, raze structures to the
ground, and so on.

seeds.name: Heretic
seeds.text:
You worship forbidden masters.
There are countless splinter sects within the Viridian church that delve
into dark and difficult territory. Gruesome sacrifice, trafficking with
Malignancies, and salting the earth are amongst the most abominable
sins a Viridian can commit, and you did so in service of the great
fecund god that moulders beneath the soil. You were cast out by your
peers, or you walked away yourself, after years of membership in:
l The Butchers, who speak the secret language of knives on pigskin, and scry with the entrails of beasts.
l The Harvest Folk, who pay tribute to Hunger and burn crops as offerings.
l The Sign of the Scourge, who seek to eradicate and isolate cursed parts of the buried deities.
l The Rosa Caelesti, who believe that Hollows are the first step on the road to apotheosis, and helped you make one.

seeds.name: Lost Soul
seeds.text:
Misery tore your faith to shreds.
With the meat-grinder of war on the horizon, and terrible
destitution both within and without their cities, the inhabitants of
the Isles are no strangers to loss; your faith was tested, and it failed.
You were a devout worshipper until:
l You discovered the wickedness that lay in your bishop's black heart. l Your temple commune was torn apart by a Hollow's cruel influence. l You saw the last war from the frontlines as a chaplain. l You were trapped in the ruins of a collapsing temple and left for dead.

seeds.name: Outcast
seeds.text:
Your beliefs saw you exiled from your community.
The Viridians are not welcome everywhere. Followers of the Old
Faith still practiced in the ruined cities of the Isles scowl at the
thought of communing with the earth, the Crown's ancestor-worship
and exceptionalism has struggled to make peace with the egalitarian
garden church, and members of the House can find the slow pace of
the sect infuriating at best. You were forced to leave your home after:
l Your upwardly-mobile Crown family publicly disowned you when they found your woodland shrine to the gods.
l House militia evicted you from your family farm and claimed it as state property.
l Old Faith Watchers burned your temple to the ground during a service, lest it attract the gods' attention.
l A noble's hunting party ran through your land, and when you protested, you were branded as an outlaw.

seeds.name: Sinner
seeds.text:
Your crimes cannot be absolved.
The Viridian faith is, on the whole, a permissive one. Worshippers
are free to marry as they choose, give thanks to the land in their
own way, and pursue an individual relationship with the divine - but
there are a few unforgivable sins. You were kicked out for good
after you:
l Mixed your father's ashes with salt, to erase his essence from heaven.
l Sold your pigs to a House abattoir to cover your gambling debts.
l Dropped your lantern after too much gin, and burned down the storehouse.
l Beat your commune elder to a bloody pulp when you found out he was sleeping with your wife.

factions.name: The Conclave
themes: Secret societies, mysteries, and hidden schemes.
Magic, alchemy, sacrifice and arcane knowledge.
factions.description:
Disparate occult scholars trying to tackle rhyme with reason
Hundreds of doctors, scientists, academics, sorcerers and divinators have sworn their allegiance to the Conclave because they share the same core philosophy: the world is not ready to accept the truth. Nestled between bloodlines, hiding behind legislation and edict, alluded to in apocrypha and woven throughout the fabric of the Isles, the Conclave has carefully guided the development of the country for the last thousand years.
They operate on principles of containment and analysis. Strange data, subjects and materials still-living rustwood harvested from Hollows, reports of interdimensional breaches, malformed refugees from curdled otherworlds are bundled away from prying eyes and jabbed, tested, probed and disassembled in order to learn as much as possible about them.
Given that Hollows are both born of trauma and spread that same trauma, it is possible for them to spread memetically through a population, so the Conclave are careful to the point of paranoia, some would say to maintain a distance between those exposed to the information and those blissfully unaware. They take great pains to secret themselves away from society at large (and each other) in sanctums, towers, dungeons, catacombs, forts, barrows and pits anywhere remote and defensible. The more important a member of the Conclave is, the less other adherents will see them, and the upper echelons are so mysterious and isolationist that many of them may well be invented from whole cloth as a distraction.
Since their creation by an ancient queen over a millennium ago, the Conclave has zealously maintained its original aim: to understand the supernatural forces that predate humanity, and eventually to counteract those forces once and for all by revealing the truth to the world. Of late, there have been mutterings of a breakthrough that they have discovered a path through to the domains of the Malignancies themselves, and a way for Hunters to survive direct contact with these vast and ravenous monsters.
Not everyone is convinced of the group's noble mission. Detractors say that the Conclave is a splintered, amoral, directionless bunch of hermits scrabbling for power in the ruins of the empire no better than everyone else. In fact, only one in six or so members possesses a solid grasp of the arcane arts, thanks to a dedicated effort on the inner circle's part to portion out sensitive information in useless fragments. The rest of the rank-and-file members are desperate posers, occult hobbyists, deluded madmen, educated hucksters, and gullible rubes.
factions.hollows:
The Conclave has a unique interest in the parasitic snickets that plague the populace they look to harvest their secrets, and turn them to their own ends. There are tricks which allow those without a Seed to step within a Hollow's borders, and wards of protection both ancient and modern give them a chance of surviving the experience. Given that only a scant handful of their number can enter Hollows without great risk or expense, the Conclave often relies on teams of sponsored Hunters to collect information and relics from within.
Working for the Conclave is no easy matter; they are demanding masters, and their obsession with cataloguing and exploiting Malignancies leads them to make strange requests. Where other sponsors may be happy to see Hollows merely burnt out and destroyed, Conclave Hunters are frequently tasked with capturing or interrogating Entities: a much more challenging prospect, and one that calls into question the nature of these beings in ways that may give their abductors pause.
factions.weapons: With their inherent connection to the occult, the Book and Staff are the primary tools of the Conclave; they give wielders the power to control, subvert and overwhelm the strange reality of a Hollow. The esoteric nature of the group's recruitment processes (and the individual idiosyncrasies of its members) result in a variety of unusual Weapons weighty recurved Swords, bone-handled ritual Knives, and long-barrelled Pistols covered in spiralling script or laden with experimental improvements.

origins.name: Crucible
origins.text:
Seekers of ultimate truths stymied by infighting and mysticism.
You were a cultist within the Temple Malignatus, and you took part
in the secret rituals expected of the most ancient order within the
Conclave. Your elders promised you power beyond your imagining,
drawn from a ravening sea of potential beyond human sight but
you spent most of your time caught up in political scheming,
arduous bureaucracy and mystic posturing. Given the cult's tendency
to glorify (and on occasion outright worship) the Malignancies,
Crucibles are viewed with suspicion by other Conclave members.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: conceal the truth,
backstab and scheme, delve too deeply into things you oughtn't, and so on.

origins.name: Geophrenologist
origins.text:
Surveyors and cartographers with an eye for the strange.
It is commonly believed amongst those in the know, anyway
that Hollows are a result of trauma visited on a person, and that
badness has a means of self-replicating into unreality when piled
high enough on one poor bastard's head. You and your fellow
Geophrenologists understand this to be bunkum: Hollows are backed-
up magic gone sour and people are merely vessels for it to occupy.
Ley-lines and fonts of power can become blocked, corrupted or
misaligned, and this can be witnessed in the material realm. Oxbow
lakes, hidden coves, unusual rock formations and cavernous voids
are all indications that something has gone awry that the visible
world has started to reflect, or retreat from, the invisible one.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: study the land,
investigate written evidence or local knowledge, hold your own against
dissenting voices, and so on.

origins.name: Knight-Alchemist
origins.text:
Warrior-scholars on an endless quest for hidden harvests.
With the correct rites and proper words spoken, there is nothing
you cannot make your own. In days long past, the culmination of a
noble hunt took the form of a ceremonial unmaking of the quarry, as
the beast was turned from honoured prey into meat to be consumed.
You, draped in heraldry from ancient houses, apply this same
principle to the world at large. The fractious orders of Knights-
Alchemist within the Conclave are prone to bouts of manic ambition
and shared delusions, and will often embark on impromptu quests
in search of new resources to exploit in distant climes or worlds
beyond our sight.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: charm folk with
your relentless enthusiasm, examine strange materials or resources,
break down or disassemble something, and so on.

origins.name: Test Subject
origins.text:
Medical curiosities and aberrations.
Destitute and desperate, you submitted yourself to experimentation
and went under the keen knives of the Conclave. After the
experiments concluded, you were left with a network of scars,
resonant metals implanted under your skin, and an uncanny
sense of the Malignancies that gnaw ravenous at the Isles. You've
been haunted by visions of unreal worlds and monsters beyond
reckoning but you believe you can find peace by delving headlong
into the nightmare and bleeding it dry.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: use your
unnatural senses, withstand punishment or torture, escape a dire
situation, and so on.

seeds.name: Adrift
seeds.text:
You lost something irreplaceable.
Becoming part of an organisation as secretive and vicious as the
Conclave requires that the prospective member give up any hope of a
normal life. Those in the upper echelons are isolated hermits, wracked
with anxiety and melancholia. You sacrificed a lot in your quest for
arcane power, but you cannot forgive yourself for giving up:
l Your family, who have no memory of you following your arcane initiation.
l Your faith, and desecrating an altar to prove it to your masters. l Your first-born, to the masked figures who granted you power. l Your one chance at happiness by marrying the man you loved.

seeds.name: Cursed
seeds.text:
You are wracked with magical backlash.
The Isles abound with curses. Pockets of bad magic lurk out of human
sight waiting to latch on to whoever has the hubris to mess with them.
Street-hawkers sell cut-price hexes ready to damn your enemies and
call down the wrath of the gods upon their heads. Most of this stuff is
nothing more than fancy words and posturing, but you:
l Robbed the sprawling barrow of an ancient monarch and watched your loved ones die.
l Stained your soul with ritual impurity that draws carrion-eaters toward you.
l Bore witness to a monstrous hound on the moor, and are now confronted with visions of your death.
l Witnessed a rival sorcerer carving your name into an execration tablet, and then watched your life crumble to ruin.

seeds.name: Hollow-Born
seeds.text:
You were raised in someone else's personal hell.
Most Hunters carry a terrible Seed within them thanks to trauma not you. You were born and raised in a Hollow and your soul was stained from the start. You may have been rescued by an enterprising Hunter, or escaped under your own power, but the Hollow resonates with you still. On bad nights, you dream of:
l The rusted mechanical womb from which you tumbled, bloody and fully-formed.
l Your father, the Lord of the Hollow, crowning you as the Princess of Thorns.
l Your brother's death at the hands of a towering black-masked Hunter.
l The writhing, protean form of a Grand Malignancy splayed above the city skyline.

seeds.name: Obliviated
seeds.text:
You have been purged from the annals of history.
As esoteric as the beliefs of the Conclave's inner circle might be, there are activities that even they forbid. You were severed from all Conclave support and communication, and your name scourged from every record, thanks to your involvement with:
l The Seven Men of Hawthorne, in hock to Dominion, who seek to oust the Crown.
l Your family: a deviant pack of cannibals who kill and eat other arcanists for power.
l The Crimson Players, a radical sect devoted to destroying forbidden knowledge and those who bear it.
l A shadowy House agency who enforce ancient pacts to maintain power over the Isles.

factions.name: The Outliers
factions.description:
Not every person in the Isles is closely tied to a faction, and some professions are common to many. Some people reject all the established orders and hold to a higher, or deeper, authority, swearing oaths to the Old Gods of the lost cities or the new order that holds human wellbeing higher than any other authority.
If you choose one of these Origins, pick a Seed from a faction that makes sense to you.

origins.name: Healer
origins.text:
Living is a messy business; dying is messier.
Beleaguered war nurse, cold-eyed experimental chemist, village
pharmacist dispensing pills and wisdom, or herbalist who invokes
the Old Gods over the pestle and mortar: however you practice
your arts, you make people better. You are more likely than most to
look past the petty details of rank, class and ability to pay: you've
seen your share of pain in the world, and you know that sometimes
there's no recovery or relief without a bit more pain first.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: deliver bad news
gently, cut through bullshit, take someone's pain away, and so on.

origins.name: Shopkeep
origins.text:
Buy low, sell high, and give people what they want.
One can buy or sell almost anything in the Isles: bread and butter,
beer and bullets, iron and horseshoes, curses, secrets and lies.
Perhaps you lugged your cart of fried gristle around your city
streets and sold sizzle to those too poor to pay for nourishment.
Maybe you draped your delicate and beautiful necklaces on velvet
pillows and sold them for three months' salary at a time. Maybe you
took cash for curses or sold secrets to the highest bidder; maybe
you just ran the bar and kept your mouth shut.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: haggle and barter,
work out what someone's real desire is, take a cut of the action, and so on.

origins.name: Smuggler
origins.text:
Dark lanterns waiting along the shoreline.
The sea is the Isles' greatest bounty, in more ways than one. Trade
routes from all across the empire built the country's wealth, not just
with material goods but also with taxes and tariffs. As the Isles have
decayed, their ships find it harder and harder to find port safely, and all
manner of strange shortages and small hardships have been the result.
You know the secret ways around the promontories, sand bars and
riptides, you know how to shroud your light so you can't be seen, and
you know which excise officials to bribe to look the other way.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: make backroom
deals, evade notice, move fast and quiet, and so on.

origins.name: Watcher
origins.text:
Fearful adherents to an ancient faith.
Before the Viridian garden temples rose to prominence a century ago,
the Isles practised a far darker form of worship. Fragmented and mystic
folk churches kept the populace safe from dozens of malevolent deities
and great spirits churches that understood that the realm of the
divine is no place for mortals to delve, and preached a gospel of fear,
appeasement and abnegation. Within the depths of lost and broken
cities, these beliefs persist. You uphold them as best you can and lead a
meagre congregation. Or maybe: you did, until you discovered the truth.
Roll with advantage during exploration when you: offer sacrifice,
de-escalate a situation, stay the hell out of the way of trouble, and so on.
